title: 教育・学校心理学
subtitle: Educational and School Psychology
educationalGoal:
Through reflection on previous learning and connecting students with the theories covered in the course, students will:
- be able to understand the problems that occur in the educational field and the background.
- be able to understand psychosocial issues and necessary support in the field.
- be able to set their own learning goals, observe learning performance and make self-assessments of their learning.
advice:
This course will focus on two areas of educational psychology and school psychology. These two psychologies may have a strong focus on the “theory for teaching” taken by those who aim to be teachers, but the course will also focus on the “theory for learning” from the perspective of learning science. Learning educational psychology will help to refine the way of learning and learning school psychology will help improve the quality of learning in school education where students are currently located. Specifically, the following topics are covered:

(1) Learning how to learn: (a) Experiential learning, (b) Self-regulated learning, (c) Expertise
(2) Cognition and cognition: (a) Meta-cognition, (b) Adaptive meta-cognition, (c) Critical thinking
(3) Collaborative learning:(a) Legitimate peripheral participation (b) the Knowledge-constructive jigsaw method
(4) School as a team: (a) Three kinds of psychoeducational services, (b) Four aspects of student support

The above contents are learned through knowledge internalization (e.g., lectures) and knowledge externalization (e.g., discussions and presentations). There is an opportunity to consider the course subjects that have been taken so far and those that have been taken in the same semester based on the content of this course.

This subject is subject to the course credit system.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Understand the problems that occur in the educational field and their background, express them in your own words and consider the implications.
(2) Understand psychosocial issues and necessary support in the field, express them in own words and consider the implications.
(3) Repeat the process of setting learning goals, observing leaning performance and making self-assessments of learning.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Understand the problems that occur in the educational field and their background, and have your own thoughts.
(2) Understand psychosocial issues and necessary support in the field and have your own thoughts.
(3) Be aware of setting learning goals, observing leaning performance and making self-assessments of learning.
